newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slightly down, awaits weaker NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slightly down, awaits weaker NY.

text.p: White sugar futures drifted lower in minimal activity on Tuesday with light mixed selling setting the stage for a lower opening in New York, traders said.
Despite some earlier buying on the dips, most values stayed on the weak side in a continuation of Monday's late sell-off in reaction to the speculative liquidation on the raws market, they said.
At 1220 GMT May was down 90 cents at $306.50, just 50 cents above its intraday low. August stood 80 cents lower at $305.80.
The nearby spread was reported to have traded at 60 cents and overall volume reached a paltry 223 lots, boosted by some 60 lots in against actuals trades.
New York was called to open between five and 10 points lower than Monday's close, traders said.
Technically, May failed to break nearby resistance at $310 on Monday, reversing lower to break trendline support at just above $305.
But the slight bounce seen late in the session brought the spot value back up to close at $307.40, down $1.60 on the day.
"The market must break resistance in the short term otherwise we may see a renewed test and break of trendline support," said Darren Gurner, a technical analyst at Sucden.
In physical news, the price reported to have been paid by Bangladesh in its recent tender to buy 12,500 tonnes of 150 ICUMSA white sugar for March/April was $347.95 a tonne.
Bangladesh is to tender again to buy a cargo of the same quality sugar on March 8 and 15.
The Paris market saw a greater volume of trading than in London at 512 lots but movements were still tight.
May was down 10 cents at $306.10 and August up by the same amount at $305.30.
